A mourner on the first day is forbidden in tefillin • and it contains 2 seifim A mourner on the first day is forbidden to don tefillin. And we learn this from Yechezkel, as I wrote at the beginning of siman 380, see there. And the essence of the bitterness is one day, therefore one should not wear upon himself the glory of tefillin. But on the rest of the days he is obligated, for behold, a mourner is obligated in all the mitzvot mentioned in the Torah. And the difference between tefillin and Torah study we explained there with the help of Heaven. And since tefillin are glory, and the mourner also all seven days defiles his horn in the dust, therefore the mourner is obligated to settle his mind to direct his heart to the tefillin. And during a time of weeping and eulogy he shall not don them even on the other days. And this is when he goes all day in tefillin. But for us, who do not don them except at the time of prayer – this is not applicable.

Even when the burial was after the day of death, and even after several days—one shall not don tefillin on the day of burial. This is not like the one who disagrees on this. And also on the day of a "near report"—one shall not don tefillin. And so too when one was buried at night, or heard at night for the following day—he does not don tefillin. But one who buries his dead on a festival, where he observes mourning after the festival, or heard on a festival—he shall don tefillin on the first day after the holiday. This appears to be the primary view. But on the second day he is permitted in tefillin, even in the morning. And those who follow the practice of the tefillin of our teacher, the Tam—shall not don them all the days of mourning. And I saw one who wrote in the name of the Arizal to don them, but Mar bar Rav Ashi is not signed upon it. And so wrote one of the Kabbalists (Birkei Yosef of Azulai), and specifically according to the reason explained in the Zohar, Parshat Pinchas in Ra'aya Meheimna, see there.
